provenance.note: EVERY heard/sent pair in this file was invented for this measurement. No recording of anyone was consulted, no dictation of anyone appears, and no line here is a real dictated sentence. Every person, company, product and place name is fictional; the only non-fictional terms are `Deepgram`, `whisper.cpp`, `Postgres` and `MySQL`, which already appear in the public wiki as the doctrine's own worked examples.
provenance.shape: `heard` is what was PASTED into the composer (the journal's `emitted`). `heardRaw`, when present, is what the recogniser produced BEFORE the shared vocabulary corrected it on the way out (the journal's `text`) — the rows that measure which of the two a diff must be taken against. `sent` is what the CEO actually pressed send on.
provenance.labels: `correction` = he silently fixed a word the recogniser got wrong, and a vocabulary entry is the right outcome. `not-a-correction` = every other reason a sent message differs from a dictation, plus messages he simply typed.
provenance.base rate: The negatives are ADVERSARIAL, not representative. Twelve are freshly typed messages that RESEMBLE a dictation in the window, fifteen are typo fixes on words that are capitalized and term-shaped, and twenty are changes of mind. Precision measured here is therefore a LOWER bound on precision in use; recall is unaffected by the imbalance.
provenance.how it is run: Each row is offered to `heard::review` as a ONE-ENTRY journal stamped 30 s before the send, so the pairing condition is measured with the rest and not assumed away. See `app/crates/richos-core/tests/heard_precision.rs`.
provenance.recall holes: Two are in the corpus as rows rather than as a sentence in a README: `buried-*` are real name fixes made inside a wholesale rewrite, which drops the pair below the pairing floor and loses the correction; `c35` is a correction the normalized vocabulary cannot hold at all.
